scope: Token-bound private seed handoff for detached Compose and Reader windows

trigger.observed: A physical mailto reply opened a Compose window with blank recipient and subject fields. The opener and child WebViews did not share the opener's committed IndexedDB record.
trigger.disposition: Do not use opener storage as the native handoff authority. Keep URLs opaque and deliver the complete seed only after the exact child has registered its listener.

compose: The parent registers its compose-ready listener before creating the child.
Rust returns a generated Compose label and appends only the authenticated opener label and opaque seedDbKey to the child URL.
The child registers its compose-target listener before it acknowledges readiness. The parent sends the seed only to that returned label with the matching token.

The child persists accepted content in its own IndexedDB and stores a label-and-token-bound session envelope for reloads. A reload can recover from child-local IndexedDB when session storage is unavailable.

A valid target receipt stops the five-second arrival deadline before a large attachment draft finishes persisting. Persist failure, listener failure, timeout, and feedback failure close the child with fixed feedback instead of leaving a blank Composer.
reader: Reader follows the same opaque token and exact-label ready/target protocol for its initial target, while ordinary same-label retargets retain the exact Reader label.

Reader session state is bound to its current label. A registration failure fails closed for both initial and restored Reader windows, so a visible stale Reader cannot remain unable to accept a later retarget.
Reader emits reader-ready only while an initial handoff is pending.
behavior.labelContract: TypeScript emits reader- followed by 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters from the first 16 SHA-256 bytes. Rust accepts the same lowercase-only form.

reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.failure: A native Compose child assumed it could read the opener's IndexedDB seed, producing blank fields in the physical OaVD6G fixture.
reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.fix: Direct token-bound event delivery to the generated child label, with child-local persistence only after acceptance.

reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.failure: A remembered Compose seed was not bound to the current child label and opaque token.
reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.fix: Store and verify the label, seedDbKey, and validated seed envelope before restoring it.

reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.failure: A valid large draft could exceed the arrival timer while IndexedDB persistence was still running.
reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.fix: Mark validated target receipt synchronously; the timeout now measures event arrival, not storage duration.

reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.failure: Rejected native feedback or Reader target-listener setup could strand a blank or stale child window.
reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.fix: Use fail-closed feedback cleanup that closes in finally, and handle every live Reader listener-registration failure.

reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.failure: Compose could not reload a child-local draft if session storage rejected its convenience write.
reviewedLifecycleFailuresFixed.fix: On a pending native URL, bootstrap from child-local IndexedDB before acknowledging a parent handoff.

slowPersistenceMutant.change: Restored the old accepted-after-persistence arrival-timer condition.
slowPersistenceMutant.result: The slow valid native draft regression failed because the child closed at five seconds.
slowPersistenceMutant.restore: apps/desktop/src/ComposeApp.tsx was restored byte-identically before the passing focused suite.

staleSessionMutant.change: Bypassed the current child-label check for remembered Compose state.
staleSessionMutant.result: The wrong-label native session regression failed because the stale seed suppressed the required handoff.
staleSessionMutant.restore: apps/desktop/src/composeWindow.ts was restored byte-identically before the passing focused suite.

securityReview.scope: Token binding, listener ordering, timeout and cleanup, reload behavior, and reader-label parity.

limitations: This is source, unit, integration, and MockRuntime evidence only.
The physical OaVD6G failure is retained as the original trigger. This repair has not yet been replayed in a native WebKit fixture.
Native acceptance must verify a fictional mailto reply shows the exact recipient and subject, warning and disabled Send behavior, opaque URLs, Reader retargeting, child reload, and fixed feedback.

The generic Tauri frontend event channel still assumes trusted application realms. The opaque iframe boundary and unguessable per-handoff tokens protect email content from the message-rendering realm.
